title: Platform engineering midweek espresso brief — controlplane routing/auth/quotas
content:
Midweek espresso brief (informal) — 2026-09-21 10:00 PT
Attendees: Maya Chen (owner), Ethan Rivera, Priya Nair, Samir Gupta, Talia Brooks, Zach Li (joined 10:08)
Duration: ~25m
Purpose: fast pulse across control plane surface — routing heatmap, auth token rotation, quota reconciliation, and the KV-cache experiment. Keep it lightweight: decisions + concrete next steps.

1) Quick status snapshot
- Routing: steady-state, but noticed a small uptick in cross-region fallthroughs yesterday (approx 0.9% of requests vs baseline 0.3%). Root cause hypothesis: abrupt AZ drain in us-west-2 triggered emergency spillover to fallback pool which uses a different model variant.
- Auth: token rotation job executed on schedule; a small group of long-lived worker tokens (legacy) failed exchange resulting in ~120 failed internal fetches during the 02:00 PT window. Failures auto-recovered after retry window.
- Quotas: reconciliation job (PLT-4912) reconciled 96% of customer counters; remaining 4% are high-cardinality customers hitting edge-case race. We have a mitigation in place (soft quota reconciliation) and will follow up.
- KV cache experiment: A/B running across 10% of traffic. Early signal: cache hit ratio improved from 62% -> 77% for short-context prompts (<128 tokens). p50 latency reduced 12ms; p99 unchanged so far.

2) Metrics to watch (today)
- Routing fallthrough rate (region/bucket) — alert threshold 1.0% sustained for 15m
- Auth exchange failure rate for long-lived tokens — aim <0.05%
- Quota reconciliation backlog — aim to clear <1h window
- KV cache hit ratio (A vs B) and p99 generation latency

3) Action items & owners
- (A1) Routing: Ethan to triage the us-west-2 drain spillover logs and produce a short timeline (due 2026-09-22 EOD). Look for scheduling/burst behavior in allocator and whether model-variant selection policy honored compatibility matrix (JIRA PLT-4827).
- (A2) Auth: Priya to patch the token-exchange retry backoff in the worker library to include exponential jitter — quick patch + canary (PR linked). Target deploy 2026-09-22 morning.
- (A3) Quotas: Samir to turn on 'soft quota reconciliation' for the remaining 4% customers and run a throttled catch-up job; monitor billing offset impacts. Runbook update required (runbook PR by 2026-09-23).
- (A4) KV cache: Talia to extend experiment window and add telemetry to capture cache-priming latencies and sequence-length stratified hit-rate. Report with charts at next ops sync (2026-09-24).
- (A5) Observability: Maya to add a short dashboard widget for cross-region fallthroughs and annotate last 72h events; include a link to the allocator events index.

4) Decisions taken in meeting
- Delay the canary expansion of the new routing policy until Ethan's triage complete. Rationale: want to ensure allocator doesn't create oscillatory spillovers under AZ drains.
- Approve the auth retry patch as a low-risk hotfix and escalate canary to 5% for 2 hours post-deploy.
- Accept soft reconciliation as short-term mitigation for high-cardinality quota drift; long-term fix to be scoped in a separate design doc.

5) Blockers / open questions
- Q1: Why did the allocator choose fallback pool B instead of local fallback A when an equivalent variant existed? (observed in two separate drains). Tracing seems insufficient; need more allocator decision logs.
- Q2: Can we confirm whether legacy worker tokens are being issued by an old CI job? If so, identify owner and timeline for rotation.
- Q3: KV cache: potential for cache-priming storm if we expand too fast. What is a safe ramp strategy?

6) Notes to self / rough ideas (informal)
- Consider adding a tiny opaque 'allocator-decision-id' to requests so we can correlate the routing decision end-to-end with tracing without exposing policy internals.
- If fallthroughs cluster around specific customers, consider temporarily pinning them to regional capacity while we debug.

7) Follow-ups and timeline
- Ethan triage + prep recommendation (2026-09-22) -> if green, scheduling policy canary expansion (2026-09-23)
- Auth hotfix deploy (2026-09-22 morning) -> 2h 5% canary -> roll to 60% if no regressions
- Quota reconciliation run + runbook PR (2026-09-23)
- KV cache experiment extension + telemetry (report 2026-09-24)

8) Quick inventory (links & tickets)
- PLT-4827: routing fallthrough analysis (assigned: Ethan)
- PLT-4912: quota reconciliation backlog (assigned: Samir)
- PR: controlplane/pull/2371 — auth retry backoff (owner: Priya)
- Dashboards: ops.redwood.net/dashboards/allocator-fallthroughs

9) freeform / scratchpad bits (copied here for context)
- small snippet from allocator logs (redacted):
  [2026-09-20T22:04:13Z] alloc-decide id=xx11 region=us-west-2 chosen=fallback-B reason=az-drain spillover-weight=0.82
  [2026-09-20T22:04:14Z] alloc-eval model-compat=false -> fallback-B used compatibility shim invoked

- rough math on quota catch-up: 1200 customers * avg 30k tokens/day = 36M tokens backlog; at reconciliation throughput 1.2M tokens/hr -> ~30h without parallelization. Need chunking and prioritization.

10) Next sync: quick standup Friday 08:50 PT (15m) — aim to close action items and validate canary outcomes.

Status: draft notes — will convert to runbook items and formal action tickets where appropriate.

-- End midweek espresso brief --
